sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Digital and ICT; banking, insurance and fintech; aerospace; pharmaceuticals and biotechnology; logistics; gaming/content and design
verified_economic_evidence: Community of Madrid investor material identifies these as regional strengths. 2024/25 presentations contain indicators including Madrid share of national finance/insurance employment and digital economy.
geography_and_limitations: Regional evidence, not a rank of Madrid municipality. The existing employer seeds need local office/workforce verification.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: ICT; life sciences and healthcare; manufacturing 4.0; mobility and logistics; creative/cultural; trade and tourism; food and blue economy
verified_economic_evidence: Barcelona Activa publishes 13 strategic economic sector groups and specific sector pages. Catalonia-level sector reports also identify significant ICT, audiovisual, games and logistics employment.
source_owner: Barcelona Activa / Barcelona city employment agency
data_period: Current sector pages; some PDF metrics refer to 2020-2022
geography_and_limitations: Use the city/metro geography indicated by each page. Do not convert Catalonia-wide numbers into Barcelona-city figures.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Technology and ICT; software and telecommunications; engineering and aerospace; business and professional services; life sciences/health; tourism and real estate
verified_economic_evidence: Málaga TechPark reported 719 installed entities, 29,018 workers of diverse nationalities and EUR 4.896bn aggregate turnover for 2025. The park is a concentrated international employment source.
source_owner: Málaga TechPark / Parque Tecnológico de Andalucía
geography_and_limitations: TechPark is a specific campus in Málaga, not the whole city. Use company directory and exact site locality.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Technology/startups; professional and business services; tourism/hospitality; healthcare; finance/currency; property and development; food/agriculture
verified_economic_evidence: The IPBN member directory exposes active member profiles and sectors; the official FIL calendar documents substantial international business/event activity. Strong ecosystem evidence, but not an official city-sector ranking.
source_owner: Ireland Portugal Business Network; FIL Lisbon Venues
data_period: Network figures current on 10 Nov 2026; event calendar current on 10 Nov 2026
geography_and_limitations: Treat member categories as a network sample, not the complete Lisbon economy. Lisbon-specific official employment rankings remain to be sourced.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Digital and IT services; business service centres; health and life sciences; mobility; tourism/hospitality; real estate/construction; retail and creative industries
verified_economic_evidence: InvestPorto says regional FDI projects created nearly 20,000 jobs in 2021-2025 and identifies leading clusters including digital/IT, business services, health/life sciences and mobility.
source_owner: InvestPorto / Porto City Council economic development
geography_and_limitations: Some metrics apply to Porto and Northwest Portugal or Porto Metro, not Porto municipality alone.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Professional and business services; property; hospitality/tourism; health/wellness; technology/startups
verified_economic_evidence: Cascais appears in the Lisbon-region professional network and IPBN member ecosystem, but current official top-sector or employment rankings for Cascais were not established in this pass.
geography_and_limitations: Treat as a Lisbon metropolitan-area submarket. Distinguish Cascais municipality from Lisbon, Oeiras and Estoril.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Finance/insurance; digital and AI; fintech; healthtech/life sciences; fashion/luxury; aerospace/defence; logistics; real estate; creative/media
verified_economic_evidence: Choose Paris Region published its 2026 Facts & Figures release on 28 Sep 2026. Its official industry pages identify clusters including fintech, healthtech, AI, luxury, cybersecurity, aerospace, mobility and urban logistics. The 2025 facts PDF provides 2023 FDI examples from UK, Ireland and Netherlands.
source_owner: Choose Paris Region / CCI Paris Île-de-France / INSEE Île-de-France
data_period: 2026 regional facts release; 2025 PDF contains 2023 FDI data
geography_and_limitations: Paris Region is Île-de-France, not the City of Paris. In 2023, the 2025 facts PDF lists UK 40 FDI projects/1,121 jobs, Ireland 7/592 and Netherlands 28/473.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Pharma/biotech; health/life sciences; chemicals/environment; digital/industrial technology; energy; mobility; engineering
verified_economic_evidence: ONLYLYON reports 16,000 pharma-biotech jobs in the Lyon region, and identifies a connected clinical, academic, manufacturing and international-group ecosystem.
geography_and_limitations: The 16,000 job figure is for the Lyon region, not the city municipality.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Digital/ICT and R&D; tourism/hospitality; creative/film; space; fragrance/perfumery; medical technology and health; engineering
verified_economic_evidence: Invest in Côte d’Azur describes Sophia Antipolis as a major digital innovation technopole, Cannes as a film/space hub and Grasse as a fragrance centre. These places are within the wider Côte d’Azur/Alpes-Maritimes, not Nice city.
source_owner: Invest in Côte d’Azur / regional economic development
geography_and_limitations: Keep the actual commune for each employer. Sophia Antipolis, Cannes, Grasse, Carros and Monaco are not Nice municipality; Monaco is outside EU/Switzerland.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Transport/logistics; healthcare; retail; automotive; ICT/media/creative; mobility; manufacturing; energy; photonics
verified_economic_evidence: Berlin’s official business-location centre republishes the 2025 Top 200 employers ranking: approximately 523,000 employees at end-2025. The top employers include Deutsche Bahn, Charité, Vivantes, Edeka, BVG and Rewe. Berlin Partner’s 2025 report provides cluster and job metrics.
data_period: Employer ranking 2025; Berlin Partner annual figures 2025
geography_and_limitations: One of the strongest sources for actual employer ranking. Top 200 covers the capital region, not only municipal boundaries for every employer.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: ICT; automotive/mobility; finance/insurance; life sciences/biotech/pharma; green economy; creative industries; aerospace/engineering
verified_economic_evidence: City of Munich business location pages identify these sectors, list local/global employers and give sector data. The ICT page notes 9.6% of Munich-region employees work in ICT; finance page describes Allianz and Munich Re as headquartered in Munich and more than 70 additional insurance companies.
data_period: Current official sector pages; some figures refer to Munich region
geography_and_limitations: Distinguish city and metropolitan region statistics. City pages offer better local grounding than national employer lists.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Chemicals/pharma/life sciences; financial services; IT/telecommunications; creative industries; logistics/mobility
verified_economic_evidence: Meet Frankfurt explicitly identifies five focus sectors for Frankfurt Rhine-Main and provides linked sector pages.
source_owner: Frankfurt Tourist+Congress / Meet Frankfurt regional business guide
geography_and_limitations: This is the Frankfurt Rhine-Main metropolitan region, not the municipality alone.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: ICT; financial services; life sciences; cleantech; creative industries; tourism; high tech
verified_economic_evidence: Canton Zurich cluster data covers ICT, finance, life sciences, cleantech, creative industries and tourism. The canton ICT page reports around 70,800 employees in 5,800 ICT workplaces in 2022.
data_period: ICT data 2022; cluster dataset latest available varies by sector
geography_and_limitations: The 70,800 employees and 5,800 workplaces are canton-wide, not Zurich city. Check the city-vs-rest-of-canton comparison on the cluster data page.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Life sciences; banking/finance; commodity trading/shipping; digital economy; watchmaking/luxury; aroma/fragrance; engineering/industry; philanthropy
verified_economic_evidence: Canton Geneva identifies nine key sectors; its page cites 313 medtech/biotech/pharma stakeholders and more than 37,000 financial-centre employees.
data_period: Current sector facts page checked 10 Nov 2026
geography_and_limitations: Figures apply to Canton Geneva, not exclusively the city. Important distinction: many finance roles may be financial-advice occupations and must be screened.

sector_clusters_supported_by_source: Life sciences/pharma/biotech; finance; logistics/trade; chemicals; advanced manufacturing; research/education
verified_economic_evidence: Canton Basel-Stadt reports 700 life-sciences companies and 33,000 employees in the sector. Its important-industries page identifies Roche, Novartis, Lonza, Bayer, Syngenta, BeOne Medicines and Moderna as regional anchors.
data_period: Basel in figures 2023 (some newer 2024 statistics); sector page current
geography_and_limitations: Numbers relate to Basel Area or Canton Basel-Stadt as identified by each source. Keep Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft and other Basel Area locations distinct.
